summary: `--here` starts a window, or a chooser, with Search Only in "Folder name" on, so a search given with `--query`, and anything typed later, covers only the folder opened and what is inside it. It needs no `--query` and works with `--pick` and `--term`. A second launch hands it to the running copy as "in_folder": true in the body of POST /v1/open, and the tab that shows it keeps it on until the button is clicked. In Nushell `fff gui` and `fff pick` take `--here`, `fff insert`, `fff cd` and `fff edit` pass it on, and `fff keybindings --here` binds Ctrl+T and Alt+C with it; the `fff gui` example that said it searched under ~/src now does. `fff pick` fails with fffinder's own message when the fffinder it finds refuses an option, as one older than the module does with `--here`; it used to return nothing.
changelog: `--here` searches only in the folder a command opens. `fffinder ~/src --query readme --here` starts the window with **Search Only in "Folder name"** on, so the search, and anything typed later, covers `~/src` and everything inside it instead of every search location. It works without `--query`, in a `--pick` chooser, and when a running fffinder takes over the launch. In Nushell, `fff gui`, `fff pick`, `fff insert`, `fff cd`, and `fff edit` take `--here`, and `fff keybindings --here` makes Ctrl+T and Alt+C pick from the current folder and below. `POST /v1/open` takes `"in_folder": true` for the same. Before, a folder given with a search was only where the window opened: `fff gui ~/src --query readme`, the module's own example of searching under a folder, searched every location, and a chooser opened in a folder outside the search locations found nothing in it. When the fffinder that the Nushell module finds is older than the module and refuses an option, `fff pick` and the commands built on it now fail with its message, such as "unknown option: --here", where they returned nothing as if the chooser had been cancelled.
behaviour_changes: New option `--here`. `fffinder [PATH] --here` starts the window with Search Only in "Folder name" on, so `--query` and anything typed later searches only the folder opened and what is inside it. It works without `--query` (the toolbar button is on before any search), with `--pick` and with `--term`, and `--help` lists it. Before, it was an unknown option (exit 2).

Second launch. `--here` is handed to the running copy. Its front tab goes to the folder, turns Search Only in on and searches. A search already showing the same words is narrowed (in the real app: 5 items became 2).

It stays on. That tab keeps Search Only in on until the button, or the scope bar's This Computer, is clicked. A later launch without `--here` that the same tab shows still searches only its folder. No launch turns it off.
A PATH that is a file opens its folder, and that folder is the one searched.

Where there is no folder. In Recents, the Trash or sent results, with no folder given, `--here` changes nothing. With a PATH that doesn't exist, a running window stays where it is and `--here` applies to the folder it shows; a first launch opens its usual fallback (the parent folder when that exists, else the last folder or home) and searches only that.

`POST /v1/open`. The body takes "in_folder". `true` does the above; left out, `false` or `null` leave the window's choice alone; any other value is a 400 reading `in_folder must be true or false, not <value>`. Before, the field was ignored.

Nushell. `fff gui --here` and `fff pick --here` pass it to fffinder. `fff insert`, `fff cd` and `fff edit` take `--here` and pass it to `fff pick`. `fff keybindings --here` binds Ctrl+T to `fff insert --here` and Alt+C to `fff cd --here`. The `fff gui` example in `help` is now `fff gui ~/src --query readme --here`.

`fff pick`, and `fff insert`, `fff cd` and `fff edit` through it: when fffinder leaves with status 2 (it refused its options and showed no chooser) the command fails with the first line fffinder wrote, for example "fffinder: unknown option: --here", and a hint naming the program that was run. Before, it returned nothing (null, or an empty list with `--multiple`), as for a cancelled chooser. Status 1, a cancelled chooser, still returns nothing, and so does every other failure.

Outside the search locations. With `--here`, a folder outside every search location is searched through a temporary index, as with the button, built at the first search. Without it, a search there still finds only what is in the search locations.
Apps. Searches with `--here` don't list apps, as with the button.

Without `--here` or `in_folder` nothing changes: the hand-off body is what it was, the window's scope is not touched, and `fff gui`, `fff pick` and the key bindings start fffinder with the arguments they did before.

Version skew. An fffinder that is still running from before the update ignores "in_folder" and searches every location; nothing tells the launch that it did. An older program run with `--here` says "unknown option: --here" and exits 2.

Manual: the options block, the hand-off bullet and a new `--here` bullet under Starting fffinder, the Toolbar row, Searching, Choosing files for scripts, the command table, and a sentence in The fff Nushell module on an fffinder older than the module. docs/protocol.md: the body of `POST /v1/open`.

notes:
Checked. Reverse-applying the src and nu diff leaves tests that don't compile (open_request, forward_open and UiRequest::Open changed shape), so I took the behaviour out piece by piece and kept the names, each put back afterwards. search_here made a no-op: all five new finder tests fail. open_request ignoring `here`: three fail. search_here before the navigation: only here_is_the_folder_the_window_goes_to fails. search_here only for a folder path: the same test fails at the file case. The server reading true as false, or absent as true: window_requests_reach_the_ui_thread and the second-launch test fail. The client not sending in_folder, or run() passing false: only the second-launch test fails. The parser ignoring --here: parses_here fails. In nu/fff.nu, seven changes (pick or gui not adding the flag, insert, cd or edit not passing it on, either binding without it): fff_nu_commands_pass_here_to_fffinder fails each time. The new finder tests also pass with SEED 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 42, 99, 1234 and 31337. check.sh printed CHECK OK before the rebase (461 passed) and on the trunk commit: 471 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. nu-check passes on the module with nu 0.116.

The real app, under Xvfb with its own settings and data folders and a copy of the demo folder as the only search location. A first launch at Projects with `--query readme --here` listed the 2 READMEs under Projects (5 without it). A second launch at Product with `--query roadmap --here` listed 1. A later launch at Research with `--query readme` and no `--here` listed only items in Research (review-sticky.png). The same words handed over again with `--here` and no folder went from 5 to 2. `--here` alone opened Projects with the button on and nothing searched (review-no-query.png). A file path with `--here` searched the file's folder. Raw requests: "in_folder": false gave 200, "yes" and 1 gave 400. The chooser with `--pick Projects --here --query readme` listed 2, and in a folder outside the search locations it found that folder's own README with `--here` and the 5 from the search location without it. After the rebase I ran the first launch and the hand-off again.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) A search that finds less than was asked for, with nothing to say why. After `--here` the tab keeps Search Only in on, so a later `fff gui ~/b --query y` searches only ~/b. That is the plan of record (leave the window's choice alone when `--here` isn't given, as before this change for a button clicked by hand), the manual says so in the `--here` bullet, and the window shows it: the folder's chip is lit in the scope bar and the toolbar button is on. A PATH that doesn't exist leaves a running window where it is and `--here` then narrows to that folder; open_request has always run the words of such a request without saying the folder is missing.
(2) A command that does nothing. With an fffinder older than the module `fff pick --here` returned nothing and Ctrl+T was dead; fixed, see review_fixes. `fff gui --here` there prints the program's own "unknown option: --here". The other direction can't be seen from the launch: an older fffinder still running takes the hand-off, ignores "in_folder" and searches everything. On macOS the app keeps running with no window, so after an update it has to be quit once.
(3) Results from outside the folder, or the wrong folder. A window that opens with words starts its first search in Finder::new, before `search_here` runs. run_search moves search_gen on and replaces the task each time, and an answer whose generation has moved on returns before it touches the results, so the unscoped answer can't land; a_window_opened_with_here_shows_nothing_from_outside_its_folder holds that under eleven seeds. In open_request the scope is set after the navigation, which is tested from Recents to a folder and for a file's folder, and before set_query, which only saves a search.
Without `--here` nothing is different: the second-launch test asserts in_folder false for a launch without it, the nu test asserts the exact arguments of `fff gui`, `fff pick`, `fff insert`, `fff cd` and the bindings without it, and the server test asserts absent and null read as false.

Doubts for the owner.
1. Staying on. It is by the plan and documented, but `fff gui ~/a --query x --here` followed by `fff gui ~/b --query y` searching only ~/b can surprise. If a launch without `--here` should search every location again, have run() always send "in_folder" and let `false` call set_scope(Computer); that also resets a button clicked by hand, which is why the plan didn't.
2. a_second_launch_hands_here_to_the_running_window runs the real program, and only Linux ran it. I read the path it takes on macOS and Windows (argument parsing, Config::load from the fixture's folders, forward_open over TCP, exit) and found nothing platform-specific, and both settings folders come from its environment, so it never reads or moves the real ones. If the hand-off ever fails on a desktop machine, a real window opens for up to 30 seconds before the test stops it; on Linux without a display the program just waits and is stopped the same way. If that is unwelcome, delete the test; then nothing covers forward_open's body or run() handing args.here on.
3. `--here` with a PATH that doesn't exist narrows to whatever folder the window shows. Not narrowing at all in that case would be as easy (skip search_here when a path was given and nothing was opened); I left the plan's behaviour.
4. The error from `fff pick` shows the lines of fff.nu around `error make`, as the module's other errors do.

For briefs still to come:
- recent-searches: Finder::search_here(cx) calls set_scope. If set_scope gets a `window` parameter, search_here needs one too. Its callers: open_request (has a window), run() and handle_request's no-window arm in src/lib.rs (only the finder is at hand there; open_window returns the window's handle beside it, so `handle.update(cx, |_, window, cx| finder.update(cx, |f, cx| f.search_here(window, cx)))`), and two tests in tests/finder.rs. Your placeholder has to follow a scope that `--here` turned on, also in a window that has just opened; it goes through set_scope, so updating the placeholder there covers it. If you factor search_for(query, window, cx) out of open_request, keep the `here` step between the navigation and the words.
- back-forward-restore-search: open_request(path, query, here, window, cx); the new `here: bool` sits between `query` and `window`, and every call in tests/finder.rs passes it. It calls search_here after the navigation and before set_query, so a live_search() snapshot taken in navigate or reveal_in_place holds the scope as it was before `--here`. a_search_sent_with_here_stays_in_the_folder expects the scope to stay Folder across a later open_request that navigates; if navigate or restore_search ever resets self.scope, that test says so. here_narrows_a_search_that_is_sent_again_with_the_same_words relies on set_scope running the search again when set_query returns early for the same words.
- restore-session-tabs: forward_open(path, query, here) has a third argument, and run() calls search_here on the finder open_window returns when args.here is set. For your gate on reopening tabs, either add `!args.here` or have open_saved_tabs return the front tab's finder the way open_window does; `fffinder --here` with no PATH from a launcher is the case.
- split-active-pane: handle_request's Open arm passes in_folder to open_request on what frontmost() returns, so with your change `--here` turns Search Only in on in the active pane. The `POST /v1/open` paragraph in docs/protocol.md was rewritten; put your sentence beside it.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: search_here goes through set_scope, so a value you clear inside set_scope is also cleared by a hand-off with `--here`, which is right. open_smart_folder still assigns self.scope directly, and so replaces a scope `--here` turned on.
- empty-state-messages: a window started with `--here` reaches No Results with scope == Folder without a click, so your Search This Computer button shows there; three of the new tests in tests/finder.rs stop on exactly that state.
- adhoc-index-feedback: `--here` in a folder outside the search locations builds a temporary index at the first search (words given at launch, or the first letter typed); `--here` alone builds nothing, because set_scope only searches when there are words. With `fff keybindings --here` every Ctrl+T chooser opened outside the search locations does this, each in its own process.
- kind-filter-single-list, regex-content-search, query-history-boost, scoped-search-special-folder-names (nu/fff.nu, tests/nu_module.rs, docs/protocol.md): Fixture::new in tests/nu_module.rs takes a name ("module" for the existing test). Two unix-only tests sit before fff_nu_commands_talk_to_the_window, with a helper stand_in(fx, name, script) that writes a shell script to run as $env.FFFINDER_BIN. `fff pick` raises an error when fffinder exits 2, so an option you add to both is refused out loud by an older program.
- folder-filter-any-kind, kind-filter-single-list, live-search-results, query-history-boost, regex-content-search, result-tie-break, sorted-search-results (tests/server.rs): UiRequest::Open has a fourth field, in_folder. In window_requests_reach_the_ui_thread the stand-in window answers /v1/open with "no such folder, in_folder=<bool>" and the test asserts on it. a_second_launch_hands_here_to_the_running_window follows it and runs the real program; anything you put in run() before forward_open runs in that test too.
- tab-bar-overflow, tab-drop-and-close: see the first item under Found, not fixed.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change):
- Workspace::move_tab_to_new_window carries only the place and the words. The new window loses the tab's Search Only in, Contents and filter, so a tab that `--here` narrowed searches every location after Move Tab to New Window. search_here on the finder open_window returns would bring the scope along.
- `fff pick` still takes every failure other than status 2 for a cancelled chooser: a chooser that crashes returns nothing without a word.
- On Linux with no display `fffinder --pick` neither fails nor exits (no output in 20 seconds), so `fff pick` waits for good there.
- A launch or `fff gui` with a PATH that doesn't exist says nothing. A running window comes forward where it is and runs the words; a first launch opens the parent folder, the last folder or home.
